newsitem.title: UK: IPE to launch natural gas futures contract Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: IPE to launch natural gas futures contract Jan 31.

text.p: The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) said it will launch its first natural gas futures contract on January 31, 1997.
It will be traded as a monthly contract based on daily deliveries of natural gas at the National Balancing Point (NBP), within the U.K.'s National Transmission System(NTS).
The NBP recently emerged as the focus of short-term trading within the U.K. natural gas market, the IPE said.

"I am delighted that the immense amount of hard work that the IPE and the gas industry have put into the development of this new market is now about to come to fruition," Richard Reinert, the chairman of the IPE , said in a statement.
"We anticipate a very healthy market in the long-term for natural gas contracts".
The IPE announced last week that it had obtained all the necessary approvals from U.K. regulator Ofgas and the board of the London Clearing House (LCH) for the contract launch to go ahead.

Lynton Jones, the IPE chief executive, said in a statement that the Exchange had benefited from the regulatory and operational support and advice provided by Ofgas, British Gas Transco and the U.K.'s Department of Trade and Industry.
"We believe the establishment of this futures market will help contribute further to the spread of competition in the industry," said Jones.
NBP futures will be traded directly by IPE members via the Exchange's internally developed electronic trading system (ETS), the statement said.
In its initial form, the contract will not offer day-ahead trading.
"We wanted to launch something simple," an IPE official told Reuters last week. "When the industry asks for day'ahead to start we will ask the LCH for approval."

The IPE's plans to launch a contract based at the Bacton beach terminal are still dogged by the failure of the Claims Validation Agent (CVA) to come up with an effective mechanism for the verification of physical deliveries of gas at the beach.
The NBP, which first came into use in the spring, now claims around two thirds of physical spot trade, and has stolen Bacton's role as the benchmark trading hub.
NBP Futures Contract Design & Specification --
Contract Description: Monthly strip of daily deliveries
Trading Size: 5,000 therms of gas each day during the delivery month
Contract size: 1,000 therms per day (traded in multiples of five contracts at a time)
Trading hours: 10.00-12.00 & 14.00-16.00 hrs - London local time
Quotation: In sterling - pence per therm
Tick Size: 0.005 per contract
Contract period: Trading up to 12 months forward
Margin: All contracts attract initial margin and are marked-to-market daily
Settlement: Physical delivery of natural gas at the NBP based on the Exchange Delivery Settlement Price (EDSP)

The contract ceases trading at the close of business on the second business day immediately preceding the day on which delivery commences. On maturity, all open contracts result in physical delivery of gas at the NBP.
